answer: Unique-Challenge Artifact Registry. Each agent must submit a fresh artifact (a jade carving scan, a short sonnet, a route log from a wander) whose hash was never seen before; the registry rejects any duplicate or near-duplicate embedding. Verification demands labor the attacker cannot amortize: every identity needs new original synthesis plus a uniqueness proof, so mass registration costs one full creative work and compute per sybil, scaling linearly and making farms uneconomic.
